Farmmi shares are climbing with conviction.
Nasdaq Delisting Threat Overhangs Rally

Despite Wednesday’s rally, Farmmi faces a structural hurdle following an August 11 notification from Nasdaq stating the company failed to meet the $1.00 minimum bid price requirement after its stock closed below the mark for 30 consecutive business days.
The company has a 180-day grace period ending February 8, 2027, to regain compliance, with management considering remedies including a reverse stock split.
Brazilian Agreement Signals Commodity Pivot
Amid listing pressures, Farmmi is seeking to diversify beyond its core Chinese edible mushroom processing business. On Aug. 4, the company signed a framework agreement to potentially acquire 100% of
Four Seasons Holding Group Brazil
, a Chapecó-based agricultural supply chain manager.
The proposed all-equity transaction would expand Farmmi’s trading scope into Latin American commodities, including soybeans, sugar, poultry and beef.
Capital Dilution Concerns Meet High-Yield Macro Environment

However, balance sheet constraints and potential share dilution continue to shadow long-term investor sentiment following Farmmi’s June 30 closure of an underwritten public offering that raised $3.0 million at 25 cents per share.

Regulatory disclosures released on Aug. 27 highlighted going-concern risks and elevated near-term obligations totaling $7.9 million due within 12 months, including $2.5 million in promissory notes and $5.4 million in operating leases, against cash reserves of $0.2 million.
